name: USER32_CALLBACK_WINDOWPROC
call_sites: message.c:925 and :985 (IntDispatchMessage, reached from NtUserDispatchMessage; user32 DispatchMessageA/W call ordinary window procedures and WM_TIMER procedures directly in user mode and use the syscall only for WM_PAINT, server-side window procedures and WM_SYSTIMER, so :925 is not reached from user32; bufsize is -1 in both); message.c:1624 (co_IntSendMessageTimeoutSingle, same-thread send, bufsize from MsgMemory or -1); message.c:1893 (co_IntSendMessageWithCallBack); reached from msgqueue.c:950 co_MsqDispatchOneSentMessage -> co_IntSendMessage for cross-thread sends
context_thread: any GUI thread (the thread that owns the window)
extra_buffer: lParam payload (message-specific, see messages-structs.md) when lParamBufferSize >= 0; lParamBufferSize == -1 means lParam is passed raw
handler_return: fills Arguments->Result then ZwCallbackReturn(Arguments, ArgumentLength, STATUS_SUCCESS) (returns the whole block); returns STATUS_INFO_LENGTH_MISMATCH if length != header + lParamBufferSize
kernel_result_read: RtlMoveMemory(Arguments, ResultPointer, ArgumentLength) inside SEH; Result taken from Arguments->Result; ResultLength is ignored; for 11 messages (WM_CREATE, GETMINMAXINFO, GETTEXT, NCCALCSIZE, NCCREATE, STYLECHANGING, WINDOWPOSCHANGING, SIZING, MOVING, MEASUREITEM, NEXTMENU) the payload is copied back to the original lParam (kernel buffer when in SendMessage, else user memory under SEH)
nests: yes: the window procedure is arbitrary user code; it can send messages (re-entering this callback), install hooks, call any NtUser service. Depth is bounded only by the kernel stack (KiUserModeCallout grows it)
result_class: C (Result is LRESULT; payload written back per message)
notes: ResultLength is not checked: a 32-bit callee returns a 32-bit sized block, so the translator must hand the kernel a block at least as large as the 64-bit ArgumentLength. The kernel WM_TIMER branch passes a TIMERPROC as Proc with IsAnsiProc TRUE and lParam as the tick count. Messages that carry a pointer payload never come from GetMessage/DispatchMessage (user32 refuses them with ERROR_MESSAGE_SYNC_ONLY), so a payload (lParamBufferSize >= 0) occurs only for sent messages, kernel-originated messages and the message hooks.

name: USER32_CALLBACK_SENDASYNCPROC
call_sites: msgqueue.c:928 (co_MsqDispatchOneSentMessage, completion callback of SendMessageCallback); message.c:1909 (co_IntSendMessageWithCallBack, same-thread case)
context_thread: the thread that called SendMessageCallback
handler_return: calls Callback(Wnd, Msg, Context, Result); returns STATUS_SUCCESS to the dispatcher (no ZwCallbackReturn of its own, so Result pointer is NULL and length 0); STATUS_INFO_LENGTH_MISMATCH if ArgumentLength != sizeof
kernel_result_read: none (ResultPointer is not read; only the status is logged on failure)
nests: yes: the completion routine is user code
notes: Result field carries the reply LRESULT of the earlier message: widen/narrow as LONG.

name: USER32_CALLBACK_LOADSYSMENUTEMPLATE
call_sites: none: the only caller (menu.c:5336) is commented out; the path is dead today
context_thread: any GUI thread (if revived)
args_length: 0 (the kernel passes the address of a local and length 0)
handler_return: ZwCallbackReturn(&Result, sizeof(LRESULT), STATUS_SUCCESS) with Result = 0 (stub)
kernel_result_read: ProbeForRead(ResultPointer, sizeof(LRESULT)) then *(LRESULT*)ResultPointer under SEH; used as an HMENU
nests: no (stub returns 0)
result_class: A (HMENU in an LRESULT: a 32-bit callee returns 4 bytes, the kernel reads 8, so widen)
notes: Dead code; translate only if the caller is revived.

name: USER32_CALLBACK_LOADDEFAULTCURSORS
call_sites: winsta.c:348 co_IntInitializeDesktopGraphics, reached from guicheck.c:29 co_AddGuiApp when the count of GUI processes goes from 0 to 1 (and again after the count drops to 0 and rises)
context_thread: the thread of whichever process is the first GUI process (normally native 64-bit: csrss/winsrv, winlogon, shell; a 32-bit process only if no other GUI process is running)
handler_return: ZwCallbackReturn(&hCursor, sizeof(HCURSOR), STATUS_SUCCESS) after LoadSystemCursors/SetCursor
kernel_result_read: gDesktopCursor = *((HCURSOR*)ResultPointer) with no probe and no SEH; ResultLength ignored
nests: not found by reading: the handler calls LoadImageW/NtUserSetSystemCursor/SetCursor; no path back into a callback was identified
result_class: A (HCURSOR: 32-bit callee returns 4 bytes, kernel dereferences 8: sign-extend into a 64-bit buffer)
notes: Runs at graphics start-up (count of GUI processes 0 to 1); low priority for WoW64 but not impossible for a 32-bit process. The unprotected dereference of a user pointer is a kernel hazard independent of WoW64.

name: USER32_CALLBACK_HOOKPROC
call_sites: hook.c:363 (co_CallHook), hook.c:389 (co_HOOK_CallHookNext), hook.c:1212/1293/1311 (co_HOOK_CallHooks, the generic dispatcher for every WH_* hook), message.c:3040/3059 (NtUserMessageCall FNID_CALLWNDPROC/FNID_CALLWNDPROCRET, CallNextHookEx path); msgqueue.c:912 (co_MsqDispatchOneSentMessage, cross-thread hook call via co_CallHook); co_HOOK_CallHooks is called from input, message, window and shell paths
context_thread: any GUI thread that has a hook installed (for a global hook, the thread being hooked)
args_length: header 1064/1096 + tail; tail by hook: CBT/CREATEWND HOOKPROC_CBT_CREATEWND_EXTRA_ARGUMENTS + strings (here Cs plus hwndInsertAfter), MOVESIZE RECT, ACTIVATE CBTACTIVATESTRUCT, CLICKSKIPPED MOUSEHOOKSTRUCT, KEYBOARD_LL KBDLLHOOKSTRUCT, MOUSE_LL MSLLHOOKSTRUCT, MOUSE MOUSEHOOKSTRUCT, MSGFILTER/SYSMSGFILTER/GETMESSAGE MSG, CALLWNDPROC CWP_Struct (1096/1160) + lParamSize, CALLWNDPROCRET CWPR_Struct (1100/1168) + lParamSize; no tail for KEYBOARD, SHELL, FOREGROUNDIDLE and the other HCBT codes
extra_buffer: per-hook structure placed after the header; Common->lParam is replaced by the offset of the tail from the start of the block
handler_return: sets Common->Result then ZwCallbackReturn(Arguments, ArgumentLength, Status); STATUS_NOT_SUPPORTED for hooks or HCBT codes it does not know; STATUS_UNSUCCESSFUL if the hook procedure faulted
kernel_result_read: RtlMoveMemory(Argument, ResultPointer, ArgumentLength) under SEH, then Result = Common->Result; write-backs: HCBT_CREATEWND copies x/y/cx/cy and hwndInsertAfter back into the caller CREATESTRUCT, HCBT_MOVESIZE copies the RECT back, WH_GETMESSAGE copies the MSG back (the WH_CBT case has no break and falls into the GETMESSAGE copy, which does nothing because pMsg is NULL for CBT)
nests: yes: the hook procedure is user code and may call any API
result_class: C (Result LRESULT; MSG, RECT and CREATESTRUCT parts written back)
notes: Contains WCHAR ModuleName[512] (1024 bytes) so every call carries about 1.1 KB. Hooks the callback rejects (ERR "unsupported window hook"): WH_JOURNALRECORD, WH_JOURNALPLAYBACK, WH_DEBUG. WH_SHELL lParam is passed as a scalar only (no SHELLHOOKINFO tail). The kernel never copies WH_CALLWNDPROC lParam payload changes back.

name: USER32_CALLBACK_EVENTPROC
call_sites: event.c:161 (co_EVENT_CallEvents), event.c:225 (IntNotifyWinEvent)

handler_return: calls the WINEVENTPROC, then ZwCallbackReturn(NULL, 0, STATUS_SUCCESS)

name: USER32_CALLBACK_LOADMENU
call_sites: window.c:2117 (IntCreateWindow, class menu name); menu.c:5340 and :5345 (MENU_GetSystemMenu)
context_thread: any GUI thread creating a window with a class menu or asking for the system menu
args_length: 12/24 (header with MenuName[1]) + Length + 2 bytes of name; when the name is an integer resource the kernel sets InterSource instead of copying
extra_buffer: WCHAR MenuName[] at the end of the block (inline, not an offset)
handler_return: ZwCallbackReturn(&Result, sizeof(LRESULT), STATUS_SUCCESS) with Result = (LRESULT)LoadMenuW(hModule, ...)
kernel_result_read: Result = *(LRESULT*)ResultPointer with no probe and no SEH
nests: not found by reading (LoadMenuW is a resource load); a menu resource hook is not identified
notes: InterSource holds an integer resource id (MAKEINTRESOURCE) when the menu name has Length 0; it is pointer-sized. MenuName starts at offset 8 (i386) or 16 (amd64).

name: USER32_CALLBACK_CLIENTTHREADSTARTUP
call_sites: main.c:728 InitThreadCallback (first GUI call of a thread)
context_thread: every GUI thread that is not a system or CSRSS thread: the first win32k call of every thread of a 32-bit GUI application
handler_return: ZwCallbackReturn(NULL, 0, STATUS_SUCCESS); the body is disabled (ClientThreadSetupHelper is commented out as a documented hack)
kernel_result_read: none; only the status is used, and a failure status aborts thread initialisation (InitThreadCallback error path)
nests: no (no-op)
notes: The first callback a 32-bit GUI thread receives, and on the critical path of every such thread: the 32-bit side must reach the user32 handler and return STATUS_SUCCESS or thread creation fails. Natural first milestone for the callback transport.

name: USER32_CALLBACK_CLIENTLOADLIBRARY
call_sites: hook.c:59 and hook.c:76 (IntLoadHookModule, WH_APIHOOK load and unload), also reached from msgqueue.c:919 (MSQ_INJECTMODULE message)
context_thread: any GUI thread of a process the user API hook is loaded into
extra_buffer: two NUL-terminated WCHAR strings after the header; the UNICODE_STRING Buffer fields carry offsets from the start of the block (the handler adds the block address back)
handler_return: ZwCallbackReturn(&bResult, sizeof(HINSTANCE), STATUS_SUCCESS) where bResult is a BOOL
kernel_result_read: ProbeForRead(ResultPointer, sizeof(HMODULE)) then *(BOOL*)ResultPointer under SEH
result_size: sizeof(HINSTANCE) = 4/8 (only the low 4 bytes are used)
nests: yes: loading a DLL runs DllMain and the API hook initialisation, which can create windows and call win32k
notes: The handler returns sizeof(HINSTANCE) bytes from the address of a 4-byte BOOL: on amd64 it over-reads 4 bytes of stack (harmless, but a known sloppiness). The module loaded must match the process bitness, so a 64-bit API hook DLL cannot be loaded into a 32-bit process.

name: USER32_CALLBACK_DELIVERUSERAPC
call_sites: msgqueue.c:1299 (co_MsqSendMessage wait loop), msgqueue.c:2144 (co_MsqWaitForNewMessages)
context_thread: any GUI thread blocked in a message wait with a user APC pending
handler_return: ZwCallbackReturn(0, 0, STATUS_SUCCESS); the body is empty
kernel_result_read: none; only the status is logged
nests: yes through the APC: returning to user mode runs pending user APC routines before this stub runs, and those routines can call any API
notes: Exists only to give the kernel a user-mode transition so that pending user APCs are delivered; WoW64 APC delivery to 32-bit code is handled by the kernel APC path, not by this callback translation.

name: USER32_CALLBACK_DDEPOST
call_sites: dde.c:231 (IntDdePostMessageHook, posting a WM_DDE_* message)
context_thread: the thread posting a DDE message
handler_return: post_dde_message(): locks the sender global memory, returns lParam, size and pvData (a pointer to the locked data); ZwCallbackReturn(Arguments, ArgumentLength, Status)
kernel_result_read: RtlCopyMemory(Common, ResultPointer, ArgumentLength) with no SEH; size, lParam and pvData are used; the kernel then copies size bytes from pvData (user memory) into its own buffer
nests: no (global memory and atom calls only)
result_class: C (pvData is a user pointer into the sender)
notes: The embedded MSG makes the struct layout compiler-sensitive: it relies on an anonymous MSG member (Microsoft extension). In the block the MSG starts at offset 4 on i386 and 8 on amd64. pvData is a pointer, size is int. WM_DDE_ACK already travels as a 64-bit portable ULONGLONG in the data (pack_ptr). Hazard: for WM_DDE_POKE and WM_DDE_DATA with CF_BITMAP, CF_DIB or CF_PALETTE the kernel (dde.c:268 and :284) reads an HGDIOBJ out of DDEPOKE/DDEDATA Value with RtlCopyMemory(&Object, Value, sizeof(HGDIOBJ)): 4 bytes in a 32-bit sender block, 8 read by a 64-bit kernel.

name: USER32_CALLBACK_UMPD
call_sites: none: co_UserCBClientPrinterThunk has no caller in the tree; and gdi32 GdiPrinterThunk is a stub that returns FALSE
context_thread: a thread in kernel GDI printing code (if ever called); no win32k lock release in this path
handler_return: GdiPrinterThunk(pkt, pktOut, RetSize) into a stack buffer (MAX_USER_MODE_DRV_BUFFER DWORDs); ZwCallbackReturn(pktOut, cbSize, Status)

name: USER32_CALLBACK_IMMPROCESSKEY
call_sites: ime.c:723 IntImmProcessKey
context_thread: the thread receiving a key that the IME may consume (any GUI thread with an IME)
handler_return: ImmProcessKey(hWnd, hKL, vKey, lParam, dwHotKeyID); ZwCallbackReturn(&Result, sizeof(DWORD), STATUS_SUCCESS)
kernel_result_read: ret = *(LPDWORD)ResultPointer with no probe and no SEH

notes: hWnd and hKL are handles (sign-extend); lParam is the key data LPARAM (a bit field, not a pointer: zero-extend from 32 bits per the Windows convention for key data).

name: USER32_CALLBACK_IMMLOADLAYOUT
call_sites: kbdlayout.c:875 co_UserImmLoadLayout
context_thread: any thread loading or activating a keyboard layout with an IME
handler_return: Result.ret = ImmLoadLayout(hKL, &Result.iiex); ZwCallbackReturn(&Result, sizeof(Result), STATUS_SUCCESS) with Result an IMMLOADLAYOUT_CALLBACK_OUTPUT
kernel_result_read: requires ResultLength == sizeof(IMMLOADLAYOUT_CALLBACK_OUTPUT) exactly (64-bit size), then ProbeForRead and copy of ret and iiex under SEH
nests: yes: ImmLoadLayout loads the IME module (DllMain and IME initialisation)
result_class: C (IMEINFOEX contains HKL and bit-fields; sizes differ)
notes: The exact-length check means the translator must produce a result of the 64-bit size; IMEINFOEX.hkl is a handle (sign-extend); the trailing bit-field word fSysWow64Only/fCUASLayer is the only reference to WoW64 inside the IME structure.
